definitions.gloss: smoking seat; smoking section; smoking area seating
definitions.explanation: A designated seat or section in a restaurant, café, or other establishment where smoking is permitted. Has become increasingly rare in Japan due to anti-smoking legislation.

examples.japanese: {喫煙席|きつえんせき}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦あります→ある：00006_aru⟧⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧。
examples.english: Do you have a smoking section?

examples.japanese: {喫煙席|きつえんせき}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{禁煙席|きんえんせき}→禁煙席：09694_kinenseki⟧、⟦どちら→どちら：00927_dochira⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なさいます→なさる：01307_nasaru⟧⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧。
examples.english: Would you like a smoking or non-smoking seat?

examples.japanese: ⟦{最近|さいきん}→最近：00881_saikin⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{喫煙席|きつえんせき}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧⟦{飲食店|いんしょくてん}→飲食店：15093_inshokuten⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦どんどん→どんどん：01261_dondon⟧⟦{減|へ}っている→減る：01985_heru⟧。
examples.english: Recently, restaurants with smoking sections are steadily decreasing.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{喫煙|きつえん}→喫煙：17580_kitsuen⟧ (smoking) + ⟦{席|せき}→席：02215_seki⟧ (seat). This word was once heard constantly at Japanese restaurants and cafés, as staff would ask customers to choose between {喫煙席|きつえんせき} and ⟦{禁煙席|きんえんせき}→禁煙席：09694_kinenseki⟧. Since the 2020 revision of the Health Promotion Act, indoor smoking in restaurants has been largely banned.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {喫煙席|きつえんせき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{希望|きぼう}→希望：00221_kibou⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to request a smoking seat
- {喫煙席|きつえんせき}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{廃止|はいし}→廃止：12483_haishi⟧⟦される→する：00392_suru⟧: smoking sections are eliminated

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{禁煙席|きんえんせき}→禁煙席：09694_kinenseki⟧: non-smoking seat
- ⟦{喫煙所|きつえんじょ}→喫煙所：07043_kitsuenjo⟧: designated smoking area (outdoors or in a booth)
- ⟦{喫煙室|きつえんしつ}→喫煙室：30778_kitsuenshitsu⟧: smoking room (enclosed indoor area)
- ⟦{分煙|ぶんえん}→分煙：20832_bunen⟧: separation of smoking and non-smoking areas

CULTURAL NOTE:
The familiar question "{喫煙席|きつえんせき}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{禁煙席|きんえんせき}→禁煙席：09694_kinenseki⟧、⟦どちら→どちら：00927_dochira⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なさいます→なさる：01307_nasaru⟧⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧" was a standard greeting at Japanese restaurants for decades. With Japan's tightening anti-smoking laws, this phrase is heard less and less.
